body.statement: Fix \(N\), \(K\), and \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\), and restrict the input to a rational tensor \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), supplied either with its exact entries or by a rational law \(p\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) inducing those entries. Characterize the cone \(\mathcal C_{N,K}(H)\) on this feasible domain and hence the label-free set \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\): equivalently, decide whether some common unit relabelling \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) makes \(\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\mathrm{id})\geq\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^{\pi}}(x,\sigma)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M_N^K\) and every \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\). Derive a recognition algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and the rational input bit length that returns such a relabelling and a finite cut certificate on yes instances, and returns arm-specific binary ordered columns together with \(\sigma\) giving a strict exact loss improvement on no instances; if binary separation is not complete, characterize the minimal finite alphabet required for a complete separating certificate.
body.justification: The feasible moment-polytope domain makes universal rank preservation a label-invariant design question; the exact finite characterization now isolates computational complexity rather than algebraic decidability as the remaining issue.
body.gap: The cut-product copositivity theorem yields a terminating exact algorithm, but it enumerates relabellings, permutations, and supports. Neither a polynomial-time recognition algorithm nor a hardness theorem respecting the balanced-law covariance image has been proved.
body.consumer: A future design tool needs either a polynomial compression of the exact certificate or a principled complexity barrier before the general nonexchangeable rule can replace exhaustive completion search at scale.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether membership in the admissible label-free cone can be recognized in time polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and the rational input bit length while returning the requested exact yes or no certificate; absent such an algorithm, a faithful hardness or impossibility theorem for this feasible balanced-kernel domain is also not yet proved.
obligation.obstruction: The exact copositivity characterization requires, in the direct algorithm, enumeration of \(N!\) common relabellings, \(N!^K\) arm-specific permutations, and up to \(2^{K(N-1)}-1\) principal supports for each cut-product matrix. General copositivity complexity does not by itself settle the restricted moment-polytope image \(\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), so no unrestricted hardness claim transfers without a new reduction that preserves balanced-law feasibility.
obligation.attempted: Expanded every ordered column into adjacent cut increments, reduced universal identity-optimality exactly to copositivity of explicit matrices \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\), and made each support test exact by intersecting every negative algebraic eigenspace with the strict positive orthant through linear feasibility. This gives terminating factorial/exponential recognition and exact certificates, but neither compresses the permutation search nor yields a feasibility-preserving hardness reduction.
obligation.partial_result: The proved partial result \(\texttt{thm:general-balanced-kernel-copositive-characterization}\) converts the universal ordered-column comparison into finitely many copositivity tests on explicit cut-product matrices \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\).  Copositivity is decided exactly by enumerating principal supports and, for every negative algebraic eigenvalue, testing its eigenspace for intersection with the strict positive orthant through exact linear feasibility.  It returns exact yes certificates, rational strict no witnesses, and the exact minimal per-arm alphabet number \(L^*(H,\Omega)\leq N\).  Its enumeration is factorial/exponential and therefore does not supply the polynomial-time recognition algorithm demanded by the open-ended question.
